Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. M. C. Pant alongwith Mr. Harnendra 
Belwal, learned counsel for the petitioners.
2. Mr. S. N. Babulkar, learned Advocate 
General assisted by Mr. R. S. Bisht, learned Addl. 
C.S.C. for the State.
3. The petitioners have filed a Misc. 
Application (IA No.05 of 2026) for taking 
rejoinder affidavit on record.
4. Misc. Application is allowed. The rejoinder 
affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioners is taken 
on record.
5. As soon as the matter is taken up, learned 
Advocate General for the State submits that in 
view of the recent judgment of Hon’ble Supreme 
Court, the petitions relating to condition of 
service may not be entertained by this Court and 
they are to be relegated to the Public Service 
Tribunal established under U.P. Public Service 
(Tribunals) Act, 1976. 
6. On it, learned State counsel submits that 
the validity of the Uttarakhand Qualifying Service 
for Pension and Validation Act, 2022 is
challenged in the instant petition and the same 
issue is involved in WPSB No.63 of 2026. 7. Replying to it, the learned Advocate General
further submits that in fact the validity of Act 
can also be considered by the Tribunal.
8. List these matters alongwith WPSB No.63 of 
2026.
[ 
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
